chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Ibn Abi Umayr from Hammad from al-Halabi from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
I asked him about the saying of Allah, Exalted and Mighty: 'And a woman who fears from her husband ill-conduct or avoidance'

He said: 'It is the woman who is with the man and he dislikes her, so he says to her: I intend to divorce you. She says to him: Do not do it, for I dislike that I be mocked, but consider my night (i.e., the night of consummation) and do with it what you will, and whatever else is apart from that is for you and leave me in my state.'
This is His, the Exalted, saying: 'Then no blame is upon either of them for a settlement between them as settlement.'

key_terms.لَيْلَتِي: Her night (referring to the night of consummation)
key_terms.يُشْمَتَ بِي: To be mocked or rejoiced over (in misfortune)

ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of nushuz and how does it relate to Khul' divorce in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies that 'nushuz' in this context refers to the husband's desire to divorce, prompting the wife to propose a *khul'* (redemption) by offering financial or physical concessions to remain free. This specific arrangement is identified as the 'sulh' (reconciliation/settlement) mentioned in the verse, highlighting the juristic basis for mutual agreement in dissolving the marriage bond when one party seeks separation.
